task: Show the figure comparing Occupational Fatalities Trends between Ohio and New York.
agent_final_answer: Successfully displayed the "Occupational Fatalities Trends" figure comparing Ohio and New York on americashealthrankings.org. Steps taken: searched "Occupational Fatalities", clicked "Explore Occupational Fatalities", changed the location to Ohio, clicked "Compare States +", and selected New York as State Two. The resulting State Comparison figure is a line chart titled "Occupational Fatalities Trends" with Y-axis "Deaths per 100,000 workers" and X-axis "Data Year" (1987-1989 through 2019-2021). It plots two trend lines - Ohio (circle markers) and New York (square markers) - both starting around 4-7 deaths per 100,000 in the late 1980s and gradually declining to roughly 3-4 by 2019-2021. Source: U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics, Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries.
